exposure: mode of delivery (vaginal delivery, cesarean section)
type of anesthesia (neuraxial anesthesia, general anesthesia)
cohort: The participants were 36 pregnant patients with Chiari I malformation (CM-I) who delivered between January 2008 and August 2022.
finding: Patients with Chiari I malformation can deliver vaginally and receive neuraxial anesthesia with a low risk of neurological complications or radiographic worsening.
mod_finding: No significant difference was found in prepartum to postpartum changes in tonsillar descent, syrinx size, or worsening of Chiari-related symptoms, regardless of delivery or anesthesia type.
